split_reasoning: Handling money, maintaining books, and conducting banking transactions are distinct activities, with money handling and banking occurring both in person and at a computer.

parts.text: Collect, count, or disburse money while serving a customer at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: The transaction is completed while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: A single payment or disbursement is completed and confirmed during the contact.
parts.work_item: one in-person cash transaction
parts.start: customer presents a payment or requests a disbursement
parts.end: money is counted and exchanged and the transaction is confirmed
parts.overlap_reasoning: Customer communication can occur during the transaction, but the other statement also covers unrelated inquiries.

parts.text: Count and reconcile cash or prepare cash disbursements away from customers.
parts.type_reasoning: The work requires hands-on handling of money away from a live customer.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Recording financial data may accompany this work, but the other statement covers data work more broadly.

parts.text: Record and reconcile routine bookkeeping entries.
parts.type_reasoning: Bookkeeping produces financial records that others use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A batch of entries and its reconciliation can be reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one batch of bookkeeping entries recorded and reconciled
parts.start: receipts, payment records, or other transaction information received
parts.end: entries recorded and batch reconciled
parts.overlap_reasoning: Financial entries share data recording and system updating with other tasks, which also cover nonfinancial records.

parts.text: Complete banking transactions electronically.
parts.type_reasoning: Each electronic banking transaction produces a confirmation or record.
parts.unit_reasoning: A deposit or payment submission is a distinct transaction relied on by the office.
parts.work_item: one electronic banking transaction submitted
parts.start: authorized deposit, transfer, or payment instructions received
parts.end: transaction submitted and confirmation recorded
parts.overlap_reasoning: Bookkeeping records can include the transaction, but data recording is broader than banking.

parts.text: Make deposits or conduct other banking business in person.
parts.type_reasoning: Taking money or documents to a bank requires hands-on work away from a computer.
parts.overlap_reasoning: A bank trip is also an errand, although the errands statement covers many other destinations and purposes.

notes: Shares depend on whether the office handles cash and uses in-person banking.

split_reasoning: The same communication tasks occur both in live contacts and in written requests handled without the requester waiting.

parts.text: Answer questions, explain information, take orders, or address complaints during a live contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The customer, employee, or other requester participates while the clerk responds.
parts.unit_reasoning: One inquiry, order, or complaint is handled as a unit within a call or visit.
parts.work_item: one live inquiry, order, or complaint handled
parts.start: person states a question, order, or complaint
parts.end: response or next step is communicated during the contact
parts.overlap_reasoning: Calls, information lookup, appointment requests, and live payments can form part of these contacts, but the other statements also cover separate work.

parts.text: Respond to written questions, orders, or complaints.
parts.type_reasoning: The clerk produces a response or processed request without the requester waiting in a live conversation.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each written request is answered or processed as an individual item.
parts.work_item: one written inquiry, order, or complaint handled
parts.start: written request received
parts.end: response sent or order processed and requester notified
parts.overlap_reasoning: Correspondence and information lookup may be involved, although those tasks also cover other purposes.

split_reasoning: Answering, routing, and taking a message are alternative outcomes of handling an incoming telephone call.

parts.text: Answer an incoming call and direct it or take a message.
parts.type_reasoning: The caller is on the line while the call is routed or the message is taken.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each incoming call is handled and either transferred or concluded with a message.
parts.work_item: one incoming call answered and routed or a message taken
parts.start: incoming call rings
parts.end: call transferred or message taken and call ended
parts.overlap_reasoning: Some calls involve answering questions or delivering a message, but those statements also cover other contacts and delivery methods.

split_reasoning: Compiling and filing electronic records differs from physically copying, sorting, and filing paper records.

parts.text: Compile, copy, sort, and file electronic office records.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces an organized electronic record or batch that others can retrieve.
parts.unit_reasoning: A received batch is compiled and filed as a manageable unit.
parts.work_item: one batch of electronic records compiled and filed
parts.start: records or transaction information received for filing
parts.end: records organized and saved in the designated location
parts.checked_by: supervisor or staff retrieving the records
parts.overlap_reasoning: Updating filing systems and recording data can include this work, but those statements also cover other system maintenance and data processing.

parts.text: Copy, sort, and file paper office records.
parts.type_reasoning: Handling, sorting, and placing paper records requires physical work.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Paper filing and photocopying overlap with system maintenance and machine operation, each of which also covers other work.

notes: The paper-to-electronic share varies by office.

split_reasoning: Completing business documents and physically preparing them for mailing are different computer-based and hands-on activities.

parts.text: Complete bills, contracts, policies, invoices, or checks for sending.
parts.type_reasoning: Each completed document is a distinct item used by its recipient.
parts.unit_reasoning: The completed bill, contract, policy, invoice, or check is the item sent or approved.
parts.work_item: one completed business document ready to send
parts.start: transaction details and document requirements received
parts.end: document completed and ready for dispatch or approval
parts.overlap_reasoning: Document preparation and data entry include some of the same work but also cover other documents and records.

parts.text: Prepare completed bills, contracts, policies, invoices, or checks for postal mailing.
parts.type_reasoning: Printing, enclosing, addressing, and dispatching paper mail require hands-on handling.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Preparing outgoing mail covers the same mailing steps but also includes other correspondence.

notes: Some offices send these documents electronically rather than by post.

split_reasoning: Operating physical office machines and using computer or voicemail systems involve different work settings.

parts.text: Operate photocopiers, scanners, or fax machines to process office documents.
parts.type_reasoning: Loading originals, operating machines, and handling output are hands-on tasks.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Copying and preparing mail may use these machines, while those statements also cover filing and mail handling.

parts.text: Use a computer or voicemail system to process an assigned office item.
parts.type_reasoning: The system is used to produce or route an identifiable electronic item.
parts.unit_reasoning: The processed document or message is the item handed to another person or system.
parts.work_item: one electronic document or message processed using an office system
parts.start: document, message, or processing instruction received
parts.end: item processed and saved, sent, or routed
parts.overlap_reasoning: Computer and voicemail operation can support several other tasks, but the machine-operation statement is broader than any one of them.

notes: Machine operation is described broadly; the actual output depends on the assignment.

split_reasoning: Computing and recording information and proofreading completed data are distinct outputs.

parts.text: Compute and record data for office records or reports.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a completed data record or batch.
parts.unit_reasoning: A batch of related entries is recorded and handed on or made available as a unit.
parts.work_item: one batch of data computed and recorded
parts.start: source data or transaction information received
parts.end: calculations and entries completed in the record or report
parts.overlap_reasoning: Bookkeeping, filing, system updates, and document preparation can all include data recording, but each also includes other work.

parts.text: Proofread data and information in records or reports.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review produces a checked or corrected record or report.
parts.unit_reasoning: A record or report is reviewed and returned or marked complete as a whole.
parts.work_item: one record or report proofread for data errors
parts.start: completed record or report received for review
parts.end: errors corrected or marked and review completed
parts.overlap_reasoning: Document proofreading also covers checks of correspondence and other text, not only data.

split_reasoning: Electronic system updates and manual maintenance of physical files or lists are performed in different ways.

parts.text: Update electronic filing, inventory, mailing, or database records.
parts.type_reasoning: Each update produces an amended system record that others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Related changes are commonly processed as a batch of system updates.
parts.work_item: one batch of electronic system records updated
parts.start: changes or new information received
parts.end: records updated and saved
parts.overlap_reasoning: Filing, data entry, and inventory work may generate these updates, but each statement also covers other activities.

parts.text: Maintain and update paper filing systems or manual inventory and mailing lists.
parts.type_reasoning: Updating and organizing physical files and lists requires hands-on work.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Sorting and filing paper records and counting inventory can be part of system maintenance but are not its whole scope.

notes: Manual systems may be uncommon in some offices.

split_reasoning: Handling incoming and outgoing physical mail is distinct from writing responses to correspondence.

parts.text: Open, sort, and route incoming physical mail.
parts.type_reasoning: Opening and distributing physical mail requires hands-on handling.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Routing mail can include delivering messages or documents, while errands and message delivery extend beyond mail.

parts.text: Answer incoming correspondence.
parts.type_reasoning: The clerk produces a written response for the sender.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each incoming letter or message is answered and sent as a unit.
parts.work_item: one piece of correspondence answered
parts.start: letter or message received for response
parts.end: response sent to the correspondent
parts.overlap_reasoning: Written inquiries and document typing can be part of answering correspondence, but those tasks cover other requests and documents too.

parts.text: Prepare outgoing physical mail for dispatch.
parts.type_reasoning: Enclosing, addressing, and dispatching paper mail requires physical work.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Mailing completed business documents is a subset of outgoing mail preparation but includes document completion as well.

notes: Electronic correspondence is included in the response part; physical mail shares vary by office.

split_reasoning: Records are consulted both while a requester waits and later in response to written or queued requests.

parts.text: Review records for information while a requester waits on the phone or at the desk.
parts.type_reasoning: The lookup occurs inside a live service contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The lookup for one request is completed and its result communicated during the contact.
parts.work_item: one live request's records lookup completed
parts.start: requester asks for information during the contact
parts.end: information found or lookup result communicated to the requester
parts.overlap_reasoning: Answering live questions includes some such lookups, but also covers answers that do not require reviewing records.

parts.text: Review files and records to obtain information for a queued or written request.
parts.type_reasoning: The lookup is completed without a requester waiting in a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The information gathered for one request is handed to the requester or responding colleague.
parts.work_item: one request's records lookup completed
parts.start: request for information received
parts.end: relevant information supplied or lookup result recorded
parts.checked_by: requester or colleague preparing the response
parts.overlap_reasoning: Written responses can use the lookup, but answering correspondence also includes composing and sending the response.

notes: Shares depend on whether requests usually arrive live or in writing.

split_reasoning: Delivering messages and running other errands are different purposes but both require movement away from the workstation.

parts.text: Deliver messages in person to their intended recipients.
parts.type_reasoning: The work requires physically carrying or delivering a message.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Messages may originate from telephone calls or incoming mail, but those statements also cover receiving and routing.

parts.text: Run office errands, such as carrying documents or making a trip to a bank or supplier.
parts.type_reasoning: Errands require travel or hands-on work away from the workstation.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Some banking and mail delivery work involves errands, but each statement also covers other activities.

notes: Electronic message forwarding is not assumed to be the main meaning of delivering messages here.

split_reasoning: Physically checking stock and placing orders are distinct activities, one hands-on and one generally computer-based.

parts.text: Inventory office materials and supplies.
parts.type_reasoning: Checking stock typically requires physically counting or inspecting supplies.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Physical counts can update an inventory system and involve counting materials, but those statements also cover other items and updates.

parts.text: Order office materials, supplies, or services.
parts.type_reasoning: An order produces a distinct request or purchase order for a supplier.
parts.unit_reasoning: A purchase order or equivalent request is submitted and tracked as a unit.
parts.work_item: one supply, material, or service order placed
parts.start: need and authorization to order identified
parts.end: order submitted to supplier and confirmation recorded
parts.overlap_reasoning: Preparing an order can involve document processing and inventory-system updates, but those statements also cover other records.

split_reasoning: Preparing work schedules differs from calendar and appointment changes, which occur both during live contacts and from later written requests.

parts.text: Prepare or revise staff work schedules.
parts.type_reasoning: A schedule is a distinct document relied on by staff.
parts.unit_reasoning: A schedule for a work period is prepared and distributed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one staff work schedule prepared or revised
parts.start: staff availability and coverage requirements received
parts.end: schedule completed and shared for use or approval
parts.overlap_reasoning: Directing clerks may use a schedule, but supervision also includes ongoing guidance and monitoring.

parts.text: Arrange or change an appointment while a caller or visitor waits.
parts.type_reasoning: The booking is made during a live service contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: One appointment is entered or changed and confirmed during the contact.
parts.work_item: one appointment arranged or changed during a contact
parts.start: caller or visitor requests an appointment or change
parts.end: calendar updated and appointment confirmed
parts.overlap_reasoning: Appointment contacts can include answering questions, but the communication task also covers unrelated inquiries and complaints.

parts.text: Update calendars and arrange appointments from written requests or staff changes.
parts.type_reasoning: Calendar updates are completed without a requester waiting live.
parts.unit_reasoning: A batch of changes can be processed and confirmed together.
parts.work_item: one batch of calendar and appointment updates
parts.start: written requests or availability changes received
parts.end: calendar updated and necessary confirmations sent
parts.overlap_reasoning: A written appointment request can be correspondence, but correspondence also includes many other subjects.

notes: The relative shares depend on the office's scheduling arrangements.

split_reasoning: Business forms, government forms, and expense reports are alternative documents processed through the same general preparation activity.

parts.text: Prepare and process a business or government form or an expense report.
parts.type_reasoning: Each prepared document is submitted or passed to another person for use or approval.
parts.unit_reasoning: The individual form or expense report is the item reviewed and processed.
parts.work_item: one form or expense report prepared and submitted
parts.start: source information and document requirements received
parts.end: document completed and submitted or routed for approval
parts.checked_by: approver, receiving agency, or finance staff
parts.overlap_reasoning: Some business documents, purchase orders, and data entries are also covered by other tasks, but each statement extends beyond this document-processing activity.

split_reasoning: Monitoring completed clerical work and directing clerks through live supervision are different activities.

parts.text: Review a lower-level clerk's work for completion or problems.
parts.type_reasoning: The review produces a checked item or feedback the clerk can act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: One submitted work item or batch can be reviewed and returned as a unit.
parts.work_item: one clerk's work item or batch reviewed
parts.start: completed work or batch made available for review
parts.end: review completed and corrections or approval communicated
parts.overlap_reasoning: Reviewing data or documents can include proofreading, but supervision also covers other checks and the proofreading tasks are not limited to subordinates.

parts.text: Direct and guide lower-level clerks in their work.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in live supervision and guidance rather than a separate checkable deliverable.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Directing work may involve schedules and instruction, but those statements cover preparing schedules and formal training separately.

split_reasoning: Typing, formatting, proofreading, and editing are integrated steps in preparing a document from notes or dictation.

parts.type_reasoning: The work produces a finished document for an author or recipient.
parts.unit_reasoning: One completed document is returned or sent as a whole.
parts.work_item: one document typed, formatted, and checked
parts.start: notes, dictation, or draft received

split_reasoning: Counting, weighing, measuring, and organizing are alternative hands-on ways of handling materials for a given assignment.

parts.type_reasoning: The work requires physically handling materials.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Stock inventories can involve counting and organizing materials, while this task also covers materials handled for other purposes.

split_reasoning: Training staff in different work activities is one live instructional activity; the subjects are alternatives rather than separate deliverables.

split_reasoning: Preparing agendas, attending meetings, and producing minutes are distinct activities with different outputs.

split_reasoning: Troubleshooting can require hands-on inspection or adjustment of equipment as well as computer-based diagnosis and configuration.

parts.overlap_reasoning: Machine operation may reveal or involve minor equipment problems, but routine operation is broader than troubleshooting.
